text:
maya: heads up — onboarding mica11b-v3 (int4) into canary today. intermittent OOMs on p4d-small during perf run, mostly under burst traffic. logs pasted below.

maya: stack shows kv cache alloc failures and then slot compactor thrash, not a clean OOM from main heap.

devon: can you paste the exact config used for the canary? batch settings + max_new_tokens?

maya: sure — default app config we used:```json
{
  "model": "mica11b-v3-int4",
  "batch_size": 16,
  "max_new_tokens": 512,
  "prefetch": true,
  "kv_cache_size": "auto"
}
```

sara: 16 seems high for int4 on that shape during warmups. memory frag + prefetch can blow past soft limits.

liam: try lowering max_new_tokens default to 256 and batch_size to 8 for canary. also set slot_compactor to "aggressive" for the short term. that reduces fragmentation.

maya: will try. quick patch:```yaml
runtime:
  batching: { default_batch_size: 8 }
  generation: { max_new_tokens_default: 256 }
  mem: { slot_compactor: aggressive, slab_cushion_pct: 4 }
```

deploy-bot: canary rollout requested for mica11b-v3-int4 -> pool-p4d-small (3 hosts).

maya: deployed patch to canary pool. starting synthetic perf sweep now.

devon: also consider disabling prefetch kv for this canary — prefetch helps latency but copies more into transient freelists which increases fragmentation under heavy conc. Set prefetch=false to validate.

maya: flip prefetch off in next run.

sara: another low-risk knob: set kv_trim_threshold=0.6 and kv_trim_interval=5s. trims big prefixes sooner.

liam: good call. combined knobs: batch 8, max_new 256, prefetch=false, slot_compactor=aggressive, kv_trim_threshold=0.6. that should stabilize.

maya: after both patches: 2000 synthetic requests, 0 OOMs, p99 gen latency +25ms, cost a hair higher but stable. logging below: "OOMs:0 | p99: 320ms | avg: 120ms"

devon: awesome. can we push a gradual rollout to 30%? need to monitor tail latencies and any quality regressions from reduced max_new_tokens.

maya: scheduling phased rollout. also kicked off a small eval set comparing int4 outputs -> no major regression so far.

sara: long-term we should add a per-model safe defaults mapping (batch, max_new_tokens, slab_cushion) surfaced in model catalog so onboards don't start with host-unfriendly defaults.

liam: agreed — I'll add a ticket to infra for a model-defaults layer + automated heuristics that choose conservative settings for quantized large models.

maya: thanks team. leaving canary open for another 6 hours and will report if anything crops up.

maya: attaching small fragments of the initial log (kv alloc fail + compactor churn):
```
[2026-03-21T14:12:03Z] ERROR kv_alloc failed size=128MB pool=kv_cache reason=slab_fragmentation
[2026-03-21T14:12:03Z] WARN slot_compactor: started aggressive pass, freed=32MB, runtime_ms=42
[2026-03-21T14:12:04Z] ERROR gen_worker: allocation failed: out of memory trying to reserve 64MB for new tokens
```

sara: perfect context, maya. we'll codify the lessons into onboarding checklist: conservative batch/max_new, prefetch opt-in, kv_trim defaults, and a smoke test that ramps traffic slowly. :white_check_mark:
